name: Energy Fuels Inc.
other_listings: ASX (EF2), as CHESS Depositary Interests at 1:1. An ASX 'Admission and Quotation' notice dated 2026-08-19 appears in the InvestSMART announcement feed
country_hq: United States (Lakewood, Colorado; city from background knowledge, not re-verified this session)
business_summary: Energy Fuels is a U.S. critical-minerals producer. It mines uranium, mainly at Pinyon Plain in Arizona, and processes it at the White Mesa Mill in Utah, which coverage describes as the only fully licensed conventional uranium mill in the U.S. It also produces vanadium as a co-product and separates rare earth oxides (NdPr) at the mill. Through the Base Resources acquisition (Nov 2024) and ASM (completed Aug 28, 2026) it is expanding into heavy mineral sands projects (Vara Mada/Toliara in Madagascar, and the Donald JV in Australia with Astron) and into rare earth metals and alloys. It has also agreed to buy the magnet maker VAC, a deal that has not yet closed.
main_products: Separated rare earth oxides (NdPr; Dy oxide in customer qualification)
Heavy mineral sands products (ilmenite, rutile, zircon, monazite); projects not yet in production per sources seen
Rare earth metals and alloys (ASM Korean Metals Plant, Ochang, South Korea; acquired 2026-08-28)
Permanent magnets (VAC; acquisition pending, expected to close early 2027)
ai_energy_commodity_link: Company-stated: Energy Fuels presents itself as a vertically integrated 'mine-to-magnet' critical-materials company. No company statement tying the business to AI data centers was found. Any AI link runs through general nuclear-power demand, and the sources making it are third-party commentary. Measurable: Q2 2026 revenue was $25.1M (+496% y/y), almost all from uranium: 310,000 lb U3O8 sold at an average realized $80.48/lb. The 10-Q shows six long-term contracts with U.S. nuclear utilities, with deliveries in 2026-2032, committed base sales of 3.21 Mlb, and potential deliveries of 3.71-5.29 Mlb depending on customer options. Two of those contracts, signed in late 2025, use hybrid pricing with floors and ceilings. Commodity exposure is to uranium spot and term prices (2026 sales guidance depends on spot-market conditions), and in future to NdPr/Dy/Tb and heavy mineral sands prices. Policy exposure: uranium was added to the U.S. critical minerals list (Nov 2025), a Section 232 proclamation on processed critical minerals including uranium was issued Jan 14, 2026, and the company holds a $725M conditional loan commitment from the Department of War Office of Strategic Capital for rare earth processing.

name: IREN Limited (formerly Iris Energy Limited)

business_summary: IREN owns and operates large power-intensive data center campuses and is moving from Bitcoin self-mining to AI Cloud Services, renting NVIDIA GPU capacity to hyperscalers and AI developers. Its main sites are the 750MW Childress, Texas campus and the Sweetwater, Texas hub (2GW, in development). Q4 FY26 (June 2026) was the first quarter AI Cloud revenue exceeded mining revenue, and the company plans to fully decommission Bitcoin mining by December 2026. It now files Form 10-K with the SEC.

Energy and commodity exposure: power-intensive Texas campuses (exposure to power prices; tariff terms not seen). Bitcoin price exposure is shrinking as mining is wound down. GPU capex is funded by Dell equipment purchases, convertible notes and GPU financing.

On Sep 25, 2026 the lease was extended from 10 to 20 years, together with a binding commitment from a 'leading AI lab' for a further 10-year term. Contracted revenue rose from $3.8B to over $9B. Rent is expected to start in October 2026

Third campus lease (15 years, unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler) and a $200M revolving credit facility
Stingray Compute LLC priced $810M of 6.000% senior secured notes due 2031 at 99.750% to fund the 70 MW Stingray HPC facility
Barber Lake lease extended from 10 to 20 years with Fluidstack and a 'leading AI lab'; contracted revenue rose from $3.8B to over $9B. Cipher bears the first $359.3M of cost overruns

red_flags.flag: Large GAAP losses and falling legacy revenue: Q2 2026 net loss ~$267.5M (including a $150.5M non-cash warrant charge), revenue -43% y/y, and negative adjusted EBITDA (~-$30M)
Heavy leverage before lease revenue ramps: ~$6.0B of long-term borrowing principal at June 30, 2026 against $24.84M of quarterly revenue, with a further $850M convert added in Oct 2026
Construction cost risk: under the Barber Lake amendment, Cipher bears the first $359.3M of costs above budget, and the tenant reimburses only 50% of the excess beyond that, over 20 years as rent

Dilution: Google warrants for ~24.2M shares at $0.01 with a $430M make-whole; the 2030 converts were partly exchanged for shares; the new 2032 converts. Shares fell ~12% on the Oct 2026 convertible announcement

Tenant credit concentration: Barber Lake's tenant (Fluidstack) is backstopped by Google only up to $1.4B + $333M of obligations. Delivery timing has varied between sources (Sept vs Oct 2026 rent start)
